title: Zoo Lions Act More Like Wild Lions With Big Meals
summary:
Wild lions do not eat at the same time every day. Sometimes they have a huge meal, and then they go days without food. Scientists in Australia wanted to see what happens when zoo lions eat that way too.

Researchers from Adelaide University worked with Monarto Safari Park in South Australia. They watched three adult male African lions. Every nine days, the lions got a whole animal to eat instead of just pieces of meat.

Eight special cameras filmed the lions day and night for three months. On big-meal days, the lions spent almost three times as long eating. They pulled and tore at their food, just like wild lions.

After eating, the lions rested for a long time. Then, day by day, they became more active again. Scientists said this pattern looked a lot like how wild lions live.

"Wild lions don't eat at the same time every day," said researcher Lesia Hryhorenko.
why_it_matters: It helps zoos keep animals happier and healthier, so kids can see lions acting more like they do in the wild.
